channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Mideast Oil Exports Rebound Even as Prices Remain Elevated
item.description: More tankers are moving through the Strait of Hormuz as shippers gain confidence, but the global supply of oil is still below demand.

item.title: NPR: This year's MacArthur Fellows include researchers who fuse science and justice
item.description: The MacArthur Foundation has just announced its latest batch of 20 fellows. Among the recipients of the $800,000 "no-strings-attached" fellowships are researchers who were recognized for their work at the intersection of…

item.title: BBC News: Watch: How did Burnham's speech go down in the conference hall?
item.description: The PM received a standing ovation as he spoke about his late dad while setting out reforms to social care.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘Online sex workers literally have to bare it all’: why Patricia Nilsson is exposing the world’s biggest porn bosses
item.description: As a business journalist, Nilsson began rigorously reporting on the power players of the adult industry, who prefer to remain in the shadows. Along the way, she uncovered how porn has shaped the internet – and our lives…

item.title: Al Jazeera: LIVE: Spain vs Croatia – Nations League
item.description: Build-up, teams and live text coverage as World champions Spain host Croatia on matchday two of the UEFA Nations League

item.title: Ars Technica: Fruit flies remember their larval diet, which influences their longevity
item.description: Eating less protein as larvae may limit their ability to produce proteins as adults.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Timnit Gebru Believes There Is No ‘Existential Threat’ From AI
item.description: One of AI’s fiercest critics believes the doom talk is about founders making money, not saving humanity.

item.title: WIRED Science: Plastic Is Melting Onto Corals
item.description: Scientists have found a new form of pollution, one where plastic and pieces of coral become irreversibly intertwined.

item.title: WIRED Business: OpenAI Delays Release of Latest Model Over Safety Concerns
item.description: The company said its latest Astra model would undergo more work to meet safety standards, and issued an apology for the way it handled the hacking of an Australian government website.

item.title: The New Yorker: How Paweł Pawlikowski Learned to Film Europe’s Fractures
item.description: The Polish director has made a career out of examining the mysteries of borders, both spiritual and political.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: How Students Journalists Broke the ‘Cornell Seven’ Case
item.description: “Our coverage was absolutely completely raw from the lawsuit and nothing was concealed. At a minimum, that’s what we can do as the student newspaper.”

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Why Is Bravo So Obsessed With Fidi?
item.description: The network’s reality stars—especially on Next Gen NYC—have given the neighborhood an outsize share of screen time.

item.title: Mirror Indy: Generations of families glide through southside skating rink
item.description: United Skates Indy held a grand reopening Sept. 25 following major renovations at the 52-year-old rink. The post Generations of families glide through southside skating rink appeared first on Mirror Indy .
